extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, department chairs, and administrators responsible for undergraduate program assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, implementing, and judging assessment programs for undergraduate mathematics majors and courses, including principles, questions to consider, and example assessment methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and integrity of assessment evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of evidence in an assessment process is of fundamental importance to its value and credibility. The integrity of assessment data must be commensurate with the possible consequences of their use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessment evidence whose reliability and validity match the stakes involved (e.g., informal end-of-class comments are useful for immediate teaching adjustments but are inappropriate for tenure or promotion decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple measures for consequential assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment that matters should always employ multiple measures of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on a single instrument (e.g., one test); combine complementary measures to support stronger, more defensible inferences about learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content principle — measure what is worth learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should measure what is worth learning, not just what is easy to measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruments need to penetrate thoughtless mastery and inert ideas; include measures of higher order skills and contextual problem solving rather than only symbolic manipulation or rhetorical repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and impact on diverse subpopulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any assessment must pass muster in terms of its impact on various subpopulations — not only for ethnic groups, women, and social classes, but also for students of different ages, aspirations and educational backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider differential impact and ensure assessment supports every student's opportunity to learn important mathematics; beware that psychometrically unbiased items can still have unbalanced impacts depending on context or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of instrument to use-case
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the means of assessment to their intended purpose; instruments suitable for one purpose (e.g., advising, diagnostics) may be inappropriate for other high-stakes uses (e.g., blocking program access).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: informal student comments are fine for refining the next class but not for tenure decisions; standardized diagnostics help course placement but shouldn't be used to deny career-program access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding perverse incentives and distortions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment systems often distort the reality they claim to reflect due to institutional policies, funding patterns, or delegation of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against rewarding delayed summative evaluation over timely formative evaluation, delegating assessment to those not responsible for instruction, slanting evaluation criteria as advocacy, or external evaluators producing overly favorable reports under promotional pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of means with intended ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Other traps arise when the means of assessment do not reflect the intended ends (e.g., course evaluations measure satisfaction not course effectiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select instruments that actually capture the constructs of interest (e.g., use performance tasks for real-context use; don't rely on follow-up ratings to infer instructional effectiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment should be broad, flexible, diverse, and task-suited
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment must be broad, flexible, diverse, and suited to the task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a range of methods appropriate to different purposes — from placement and grading to program review — tailoring choices to context and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclic assessment process (set goals → improve)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cycle of setting learning goals, designing instructional strategies, determining assessment methods, gathering data, and using the results to improve the major.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the assessment cycle in mind: decide goals, choose methods that let you judge goal attainment, administer, compile/analyze data, report results, revise goals/methods, and repeat; students should be kept informed of purposes and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open process beginning with clear goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment systems should be an open process, beginning with goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make goals explicit and transparent as the foundation for selecting methods and interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures must enhance students' mathematical performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should measure and enhance students' mathematical performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessment not only to judge but also to drive improvement in student learning; results should inform instruction and curriculum changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw valid inferences from multiple instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment should draw valid inferences from multiple instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triangulate across instruments to strengthen claims about student learning; be cautious about overinterpreting single measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder involvement in goal-setting and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Who has a voice in setting goals and in determining the nature of the assessment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant stakeholders (faculty, students, employers, advisors) in defining outcomes and assessment design to increase relevance, buy-in, and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground assessment in relevant research literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the faculty ground assessment in relevant research from the professional literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use research-based principles and validated instruments where possible rather than relying solely on ad hoc practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify all outcomes, including indirect ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Have all outcomes been identified — including those that are indirect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document both direct learning outcomes and indirect/collateral effects (e.g., changes in student attitudes, departmental reputation) so assessments can capture the full footprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect unintended outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the means of assessment likely to identify unintended outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods that can reveal side-effects (positive or negative) of instruction or policy, not only intended effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess relevance of mathematics for students' needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the mathematics assessed important for the students in the program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assessed content aligns with students' future contexts and aspirations (science, education, business, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine contexts and populations of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: In what contexts and for which students is the program particularly effective?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze assessment results by context/subpopulation to identify where practices work or need adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support faculty leadership and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the assessment program support development of faculty leadership?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster faculty involvement and ownership; successful assessment requires intense local faculty engagement and committed leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use findings to improve instruction and programs
rubrics_metrics.description: How are the results of the assessment used for improving education?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate findings into concrete instructional, curricular, or programmatic changes and close the loop by re-assessing after changes are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ a wide array of assessment methods (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A plethora of other methods ... enhance the options for assessment of students and programs: (capstone courses; comprehensive exams; core exams; diagnostics; external examiners; employer advisors; feedback from graduates; focus groups; group projects; individual projects; interviews; journals; oral exams; performance tasks; portfolios; research projects; samples of student work; senior seminars; senior theses; surveys; visiting committees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these methods as appropriate to different purposes (placement, grading, program review, summative judgments) and contexts; mix methods to address varied goals and to provide multiple lines of evidence.
